question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(8,0.7),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{x}){(0.7)}^{x}{(0.3)}^{8-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X\le 6)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,2,…,6.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X>6)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=7,8,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X>6),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6) & =P(X\in \{7,8\}) \\  & =f(7)+f(8) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{7}){(0.7)}^{7}{(0.3)}^{8-7}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{8}){(0.7)}^{8}{(0.3)}^{8-8} \\  & =8{(0.7)}^{7}{(0.3)}^{1}+1{(0.7)}^{8}{(0.3)}^{0} \\  & ≈0.255\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 6) & =1-P(X>6) \\  & ≈1-0.255 \\  & =0.745\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
